Priya: To start, how do you usually get to the grocery store?
Marcus: The number 12 bus is my only option, and when the bus cuts service I have no way to get to the grocery store at all.
Priya: What happens when the bus route changes?
Marcus: When the bus route changed last spring the trip to the grocery store went from twenty minutes to over an hour, because the bus route no longer stops near my street.
Priya: How does the bus schedule affect your shopping?
Marcus: The bus schedule ends early on Sundays, so if I miss the last bus I cannot get home from the grocery store with my bags.
Priya: Is there a store within walking distance?
Marcus: Walking distance is not real here; the grocery store is three miles away and the bus is the only way to cover that distance.
Priya: How do you plan around the bus for big shopping trips?
Marcus: I plan every shopping trip around the bus timetable, because carrying groceries on the bus for an hour is exhausting.
Priya: What did you do when the bus went on strike?
Marcus: During the bus strike I paid for rides to the grocery store, and those rides cost more than the food itself.
Priya: Does the bus run often enough for fresh food shopping?
Marcus: The bus comes once an hour, so fresh food shopping means waiting at the stop with melting frozen items on the way home.
Priya: If the bus ran more often, what would change?
Marcus: If the bus ran every fifteen minutes I would shop for fresh food twice a week instead of one heavy grocery store trip a week.
